notes: With the files in a bucket (storage "s3") GET /api/downloads/{id} answers 409 s3_no_zip: the files are downloaded one by one, each from its link; POST still gives the paths for saving into a folder. Several files as one ZIP. 1 to 10000 ids (400 bad_request otherwise); files not in the library are left out, and with none left 404 not_found. files is the archive's order, with each file's path inside it, its day folder as on the server, and before it the folder's directory when the files come from several folders (Family/2026-09-27/IMG_0001.jpg); saving into a folder uses the same paths. Files in folders the caller doesn't see are left out. name is the server's name, or the folder's when all files come from one folder and the caller sees others too, and the day the files arrived, or today. GET /api/downloads/{id} (also HEAD) sends the ZIP: application/zip, stored without compression, Zip64 when needed, exactly size bytes, a strong ETag, Range and If-Range; Cache-Control private, no-store, no-transform. Only the person (or PIN session, for a PIN that shows its folder) who asked can fetch it; it is gone a day after its last use or after a restart (404 not_found). A file deleted meanwhile is left out, which changes the ETag, so a resumed download starts over. When two of the person's ZIPs or four in all are being sent, 503 busy with Retry-After.
